target_customer: Trucking fleets running Class 8 diesel semis, such as Ryder, that want lower fuel cost and emissions without buying electric tractors
problem: Battery-electric semis are expensive and diesel fleets need fuel savings now. Revoy sells a swappable electric dolly that sits between tractor and trailer so a diesel truck becomes a hybrid in minutes.
business_model: Hardware as a service, fleets pay per mile with fees tied to diesel saved and nothing up front
product_category: Hybrid-electric add-on dolly for diesel semi trucks

founders.name: Ian Rust
founders.role: Co-founder and CTO (YC page lists him as the only founder; Electrek calls him founder)
founders.background_notes: Source: YC company page. Ventureburn calls him Revoy's first hire and an early Cruise engineer.

founders.name: Peter Reinhardt
previous_startups: Segment (sold to Twilio, reported at $3.2 billion)
founders.background_notes: Named by Ventureburn and Carscoops as CEO. He is not on the YC page, so his start date at Revoy is not confirmed.

competitors.name: Hyliion
competitors.what: Hybrid-electric axle system for long haul trucks, a tractor side approach to electrifying diesel Class 8 trucks
competitors.traction_then: Fleets including Ryder were reported testing its electric axle
competitors.funding_then: Publicly listed by 2020, amount not checked

technical_complexity.rationale: A swappable battery dolly with drive axle, coupling to existing tractors, fleet safety and integration. Needed hardware engineering and field validation by a tiny team.

defensibility.rationale: Patented-style hardware and a per-mile service with swap stations would be slow to copy, but rival trailer e-axle makers pursue similar efficiency gains. No patent was verified.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Truck makers focused on battery-electric tractors. Revoy ran a year-long pilot with Ryder and raised a $27M Series A in 2026 (Electrek, Ventureburn). No incumbent copy was found.

market_need_then: Diesel fleets faced fuel cost and emissions pressure while battery-electric semis such as the Volvo VNR Electric and Freightliner eCascadia were costly (Electrek 2026 compares range and weight). The YC page claims $25k more profit per truck per year, a company claim.

branding.domain_note: Uses revoy.com per the YC page.

identity.visual_style: Plain B2B freight site with tagline Electric freight that actually works
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and practical, focused on cost per mile

rebrands.why: Not stated. CB Insights lists SixWheel as the former name and the YC page still carries the SixWheel pitch.

brand_strength.rationale: Trade press covers the product, not the brand. The rename date and reason are not public in sources found.

outcome_analysis: Revoy started as SixWheel in 2020, joined YC in Winter 2022, ran a year-long Ryder pilot and then raised a $27M Series A in July 2026 led by Standard Capital, bringing reported total funding above $41M. The no-upfront per-mile model lowers the barrier for fleets, and the company still has to prove deployments beyond the first Pacific Northwest route and swap stations.
notes: Series A stated by Ventureburn (July 31, 2026) and Electrek (Aug 2026, via Dealroom). Ventureburn says total raised is over $41M, so earlier rounds exist. Aggregators (CB Insights about $4.5M over 6 rounds, VCBacked seed Jan 2023) conflict and are unverified, so no seed round is recorded. Titles conflict: Electrek calls Rust CEO. Competitor search for dated 2022 rivals found little. Range Energy, Trailer Dynamics and eTruck results were undated or later and are not listed. No outcome events (layoffs, shutdown) found. Name origin not found.
